description: "replication of <organism>" word order. BIOLOGICAL only covers "<organism> replication", so virology abstracts phrased "the replication of enteroviruses" passed the filter — one duplicated cluster of these accounted for 106 of the 501 rows Stage 3 later screened out as not-a-replication. Up to three filler words are allowed before the organism ("Replication of Oncolytic Herpes Simplex Virus"). cell/cellular/parasite are split out and must be the HEAD of the phrase — followed by punctuation, end, or a preposition/verb. They have common non-biological collocations, and with a three-word filler window the unrestricted form killed genuine replications outright: "a direct replication of the classic CELL PHONE driving study" and "a conceptual replication of the PARASITE STRESS theory of values" both became false_positive, which is terminal. The unambiguous organism terms need no such restriction. The filler window also refuses study-nouns, so "a replication of the original STUDY in cells" keeps its real head ("study") and survives. Without that, a replication merely CONDUCTED in biological material was excluded. SHADOW: the original refuses study-nouns inside the three-word filler with a negative lookahead, which RE2 cannot express; dropping it widens the discard ('replication of the original study of DNA repair' would now match). The cell/cellular/parasite head restriction IS preserved faithfully by consuming what the original looked ahead at. keyword_verdict() keeps the exact original via pyre_regex. Loaded back into keyword_verdict() as pattern id BIOLOGICAL_OF (filter/phrase_detection.py).

measured.rationale: One duplicated virology cluster phrased 'the replication of <organism>' accounted for 106 of the 501 rows Stage 3 later screened out as not-a-replication — the measurement that motivated the pattern. It says nothing about the widened RE2 form, which is why this spec is shadow.
